title: Dooars safari planning: Jaldapara or Gorumara
meta_description: Jaldapara or Gorumara for a Dooars safari: how the parks differ, jeep and watchtower safaris, indicative costs, booking, season dates and who each suits.
summary: Choose Jaldapara for the best chance of one-horned rhinos on open grassland jeep safaris, and Gorumara for watchtower safaris close to Siliguri and an easy weekend. Both parks close from 16 June to 15 September, and the best sightings come from December to April. With four nights, do both.
key_takeaways: Jaldapara, about 216 km², has the largest population of one-horned rhinos in West Bengal and is best for jeep safaris across grassland.
Gorumara, about 80 km² and only 80 km from Siliguri, is known for watchtower safaris such as Jatraprasad and Medla.
Safaris are priced per jeep for up to six people, so sharing a vehicle cuts the cost sharply.
All Dooars national parks close from 16 June to 15 September every year.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: The Dooars are the forested foothills of North Bengal, between the Teesta river and the Assam border, where tea gardens, rivers and national parks lie below the Bhutan hills. Two parks draw most visitors: Jaldapara near Madarihat and Gorumara near Lataguri. Both have one-horned rhinoceros, Asian elephants, gaur and a rich list of birds, and both are run by the West Bengal forest department.

They feel quite different, though. Jaldapara is larger and more open, and its jeep safaris drive across grassland in search of rhinos. Gorumara is smaller and closer to Siliguri, and most of its trips take you to a watchtower where you wait quietly for animals to come to a salt lick or water hole. If you want rhinos, choose Jaldapara. If you want an easy, short break with a good chance of gaur and elephants, choose Gorumara. If you have four nights, do both.
Park rules, fees and safari quotas change from season to season. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Jaldapara: the rhino park
paras: Jaldapara National Park spreads along the Torsa river near Madarihat, about 125 km from Siliguri. It has the largest population of one-horned rhinoceros in West Bengal, and its tall grassland is where you are most likely to see them in the open. Jeep safaris follow set forest routes with a guide, usually lasting 1.5–2 hours, and also turn up elephants, gaur, hog deer, peafowl and, in winter, storks and ducks along the river.

Elephant safaris used to be the classic Jaldapara experience. They have been suspended and restarted more than once in recent years, and the old Hollong forest lodge was destroyed by fire in June 2024. When they run, only a small number of seats are sold online, at about ₹1,000–2,500 per person. Some travellers choose not to ride elephants for welfare reasons. Plan around jeep safaris and treat an elephant ride as a possible extra. Check current status before you travel.
Stay two nights in Madarihat for two or three safaris. Totopara, home of the Toto community, is about 22 km north, and Chilapata forest is close by for a quieter drive to the ruins of Nal Raja Garh.

sections.heading: Gorumara: watchtowers and an easy weekend
paras: Gorumara National Park lies near Lataguri, only about 80 km and 2–2.5 hours from Siliguri, which makes it the easiest park for a short break. Most of its trips are watchtower safaris. A jeep takes you into the forest to a tower, you climb up and you wait while animals come to a salt lick or water body below. Jatraprasad, named after a forest department elephant, overlooks a grassland where rhinos and gaur often come. Medla adds a short bullock-cart ride and a performance by Adivasi dancers at the camp. Chandrachur is quieter, and Chukchuki is mainly for birds.

Gorumara suits families and anyone who prefers sitting still to driving around. Sightings depend on patience and luck, and the Murti riverbed at dusk is a pleasant walk after the afternoon slot. Lataguri has rooms for every budget, from simple lodges at ₹1,200–2,500 a night to resorts at ₹3,000–7,000, and the WBFDC lodge at Murti is a short drive away.

sections.heading: Booking safaris and what they cost
paras: All safaris in the Dooars parks are run by the West Bengal forest department, not by private operators. The department sells a fixed number of jeep slots for each route and time of day. In recent seasons many slots have been sold online a few weeks ahead through the official forest department and West Bengal Forest Development Corporation (WBFDC) pages, with the rest sold at the counters in Lataguri and Madarihat, often from the afternoon before.

Because safaris are priced per jeep for up to six people, couples and solo travellers save a great deal by sharing. Lodges often put guests together, and you can ask at the counter whether anyone wants to share. A full jeep at Jaldapara costs about ₹3,000–4,500, so six people sharing pay ₹500–750 each.
list: Start planning four to six weeks ahead for November to March, and earlier for Puja, Christmas and New Year.
Use only official booking pages, and be wary of anyone selling guaranteed slots.
Carry the same photo ID you used to book, and report 15–30 minutes before your slot.
Choose the first morning slot for animals and birds, and the last afternoon slot for warm light.
Tip the guide and driver if they did well; ₹100–200 each per safari is usual.

sections.heading: When to go
paras: Every national park and wildlife sanctuary in North Bengal closes for the monsoon from 16 June to 15 September, for the breeding season and because rain washes out forest tracks. Tea-garden villages such as Samsing stay open, but there are no safaris. The parks reopen on 16 September, though some routes open later if tracks need repair.

October brings the Durga Puja holidays, when slots sell out quickly and the grass is still tall enough to hide rhinos. From December to April the grass is shorter, the forest drier and sightings better. Dawn in an open jeep from November to February is cold, around 8–12°C, so wear layers, a hat and gloves. Parks can also close for a day or two for animal counts, elections or after a forest fire. Check current status before you travel.

For birdwatchers, winter is best of all. Migrant ducks and storks gather along the Torsa and Murti, and hornbills feed in the fruiting trees at the forest edge. Spring brings hotter afternoons by April, so plan safaris for early morning and rest in the middle of the day.

sections.heading: Doing both parks in one trip
paras: The two parks are about 75 km and 2 hours apart by car, so they combine easily. Our four-night rhino trail spends two nights at Gorumara and two at Jaldapara, with three or four safaris, a visit to Totopara and a tea estate. It starts at ₹12,000 per person on the Budget tier, ₹22,000 on Value and ₹38,000 on Comfort.

For a weekend, the two-night trip with one night in the tea hills at Samsing and one at Lataguri starts at ₹6,500 per person. With six nights, our loop continues east from Jaldapara to Buxa, where walks to Buxa Fort and Jayanti replace the classic safari.
Dress in dull greens, browns or greys, keep voices low and never ask the driver to chase animals. Binoculars make a big difference, as rhinos and elephants are often seen at a distance.

faqs.q: Which is better for rhinos, Jaldapara or Gorumara?
faqs.a: Jaldapara. It has the largest population of one-horned rhinoceros in West Bengal, and its jeep safaris cross open grassland where rhinos are often seen. Gorumara also has rhinos, usually seen from watchtowers such as Jatraprasad, but sightings depend more on luck. For the best chance, take two or three safaris at Jaldapara between December and April.

faqs.q: When are Jaldapara and Gorumara closed?
faqs.a: Both parks, like every national park and wildlife sanctuary in North Bengal, close from 16 June to 15 September every year for the monsoon and the breeding season. They reopen on 16 September, though some routes open later if tracks need repair. Parks can also close for a day or two at short notice. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much does a jeep safari cost in the Dooars?
faqs.a: Safaris are priced per jeep for up to six people, including the vehicle, driver, forest guide and entry fees. Indicative costs are about ₹3,000–4,500 at Jaldapara, ₹2,500–3,500 for a Gorumara watchtower trip and ₹2,800–3,800 for Medla with the bullock cart. Foreigners pay higher entry fees, and some parks charge a camera fee.

faqs.q: Can I book a Dooars safari on arrival?
faqs.a: Often, yes, outside peak weeks. Slots not sold online are usually sold at the forest department counters in Lataguri and Madarihat, often from the afternoon before. Queues start early in peak season, and Puja, Christmas and New Year weeks sell out. Guests in WBFDC lodges can sometimes book at reception. Book online ahead for those busy weeks.

faqs.q: How many nights do I need for a Dooars safari trip?
faqs.a: Two nights at one park gives you two or three safaris, which is enough for a good chance of rhinos and elephants. Four nights lets you do both Gorumara and Jaldapara, with Totopara and a tea estate. A weekend of two nights works well from Siliguri if you combine Samsing with one Gorumara safari.
